author: Tazz
body:
Hello.

Why do staff ban for excessive infractions? They've got their punishment and they've served their time for it. It's like telling a man that he has to prison because he has been 20 times already. That is honestly stupid. Funnily enough, you can not be aware of the fact you can be banned for excessive infractions as it is not in the rules.

Thanks

title: Banning for Excessive Infractions

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
If someone has multiple warns, kicks and tempbans and are still breaking the rules, they obviously have not learnt their lesson and are a detriment to the community.

Personally, I think the excessive infractions ruleset is quite lenient as is...20 infractions, if you haven't learnt your lesson by then, then you're not fit to interact with this community.

You shouldn't have to worry about being banned for excessive infractions if you do the most simple thing in the world.
Follow the rules.

If you do this, then we won't have a problem.

replies.author: Matic0B
replies.body:
If someone is warned, kicked and temp. banned for the same thing, just ban him next time for good instead of letting him get 20 infractions.

I think people with 20+ infractions deserve some sort of punishment but really if you just didn't temp ban for hacking and would stick to warn->kick->temp->perma then it would be avoided.

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
Although I do agree with you to some extent, it's not that simple.

Most of the time, the time period between infractions is too great to give a perma-ban to someone straight up. Despite them having a warn, kick and temp-ban.

What if those 3 infractions are 10 months old? Would it be just to perma-ban someone when this is the first time they've reoffended in months?

No, which is why a more lenient punishment is given out.

Because of this, users can rake up quite a few infractions without being permanently banned.
This is why the excessive infractions punishment is currently active.

replies.body: Warns and kicks are like tickets and fines. If you repeat certain offences to an extent, you're going to eventually get jailed or heavily punished for your actions. Like mentioned above, a temporary ban after 20 infractions is pretty lenient - You've been given 20 chances to abide the rules, which is quite a lot once you think about it, but you will have actions taken on your refusal to follow them if you still continue to cause disruption.

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
Correct, you give out a more lienant punishment because if the long time period from the present and the time of the last infraction.

But when there're several months between infractions, despite the player reoffending, it's simply too harsh to give out a permanent ban for one situation.

Because of this, players can get a lot of infractions without getting perma-banned.

The excessive infraction rule is then executed because clearly, after 20 infractions, the player has not learnt their lesson and shows no signs of improving.

replies.author: awesome_apricot
replies.body:
If someone is swearing on the street and a policeman warns them, and they stop it's good (warn/kick).
If they carry on, they may warn them again and if they don't stop they may take them to a cell for the night at the police station (temp ban).
If they leave and start mouthing off then they may find themselves in further trouble.
At the end of the day we don't want people on the server that are rude and do not follow the rules as it spoils the fun for everyone else, and the punishments in place are reasonable and fair.
